clue.text: Indispensable part of army is completely surrounded

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British Army

indicators.note: the word for completely is wrapped around the clue's own little word is

parts.note: completely means quite, as in 'quite right'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some vital unit of the army finds itself encircled by the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded' looks like the army's plight but signals the container; RE is the usual crossword shorthand for the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A requisite thing is essential, a synonym for indispensable.

clue.text: State line briefly adopted by lots of papers

indicators.note: the short form of line is taken into the word for lots of papers

parts.note: a ream is a large quantity of paper, 500 sheets
L is the abbreviation for line, briefly signals the short form

explanation.surface: A national policy is briefly taken up by many newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' puts L inside REAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or state ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Sweet, but does she rule over doltish types?

definitions.meaning: a dessert, a baked British pudding of breadcrumbs, jam and meringue

definitions.text: does she rule over doltish types?
definitions.meaning: puddings can mean stupid people, so a female ruler of them would be their queen

explanation.walkthrough: Pudding is a British word for both a dessert and a dull-witted person.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a traditional British dessert and, read literally, a woman ruling over fools.

clue.text: I had one damaged boot — vote to get a set

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a cross, X, is marked on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: Someone with a broken boot casts a vote to win a television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges BOOT into OTBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiot box is slang for a television, the set in the living room.

clue.text: Goes over again changes made in treaties

indicators.note: the letters of the word are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A negotiator repeats the revisions made to some international agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes made in' rearranges TREATIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat, so iterates means does or goes over again.

clue.text: TV channel upset about inventor

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: side is old British slang for a TV channel, as in 'turn over to the other side'
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A television station is annoyed about a creator of devices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SIDE into EDIS. Thomas Edison invented the phonograph and electric light bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was a famous American inventor, so the name is an example of the category.

clue.text: Duck on gloomy river

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the duck's letter follows

parts.note: dour means sullen and gloomy
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: A duck is sitting on a dismal river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Douro flows through Spain and Portugal to the sea at Porto.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douro is a major Iberian river, so this is an example of the class named.

clue.text: Retire from race after defending record

indicators.note: the race's word guards the record by surrounding it

parts.note: to dart is to race or dash
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An athlete quits the race after defending a title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like a sporting title but is a disc; 'after defending' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to leave or withdraw, as to retire from a room.

clue.text: Basic decision that's up for review

indicators.note: to review is to look over and revise, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the contraction that's gives the letters THATS

explanation.surface: A judgment that is being reconsidered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for review' rearranges DECISION THAT'S UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsophisticated means simple and unrefined, the same as basic.

clue.text: Speech about form of exercise — running?

indicators.note: the speech's word goes around the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
PE is physical education, a form of exercise

explanation.surface: A talk about a type of workout asks whether it means jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' looks like jogging but means working, as a machine runs; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine in operation is running, so the running of something is its operation.

clue.text: A biography covering end of romance with swimmer

indicators.note: the biography's word sits over and around the other letters, covering them

parts.note: a life is a written account of someone's life story

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A life story wraps around a love affair's conclusion featuring someone who swims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts E (end of romance) and W inside LIFE, after A. 'Swimmer' looks like a person; here it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The alewife is a North American fish of the herring family, so it is a swimmer.

clue.text: Stalling of negotiations as one representative finds advantage lessened

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

indicators.note: the word for advantage is made smaller by losing its last letter

parts.note: an asset is something that gives an advantage

explanation.surface: Talks stall when a delegate discovers their edge has been reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lessened' trims the final T from ASSET, leaving ASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock where talks can make no progress.

clue.text: He painted "Old lady with bag"

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, giving MA
to bag something is to net or catch it

explanation.surface: Someone names the title of a portrait of an elderly woman with a handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes make it look like a picture's title; the words are wordplay. Edouard Manet was a French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Edouard Manet was a French nineteenth-century artist, so he is a man who painted.

clue.text: Happy or upset about chapter on a set of disputed writings

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for chapter
upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful or troubled about a chapter in a contested body of texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HAPPY OR into APORYPH; 'about' puts C inside it to make APOCRYPH, and 'on' adds A after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are biblical or other texts of doubtful authenticity, whose canonical status is disputed.

clue.text: Remaining newt protected by partner

indicators.note: the newt's word is shielded by being placed inside the partner's word

parts.note: a lover is a romantic partner
an eft is a newt, especially a young one

explanation.surface: A newt survives because its mate guards it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' signals the container; 'Remaining' reads as surviving but is the adjective for surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover means remaining or surplus after the rest has been used.

clue.text: Heck! Iris distraught after lover's beginning to be lecherous

indicators.note: after says the jumbled letters come after the first letter
a word's beginning is its first letter
distraught means upset, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Iris is distressed after a suitor starts to become lustful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distraught' signals the anagram, and 'after' puts the jumbled letters behind the first letter of lover's; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lickerish is an old word meaning lustful or lewd.

clue.text: Baby twins, say, about to be abandoned

indicators.note: these letters are to be dropped from the zodiac word

parts.note: Gemini, the Twins, is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: about signals that the abbreviation for say is turned round

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: Infant twins are about to be left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns EG into GE, and 'to be abandoned' drops GE from GEMINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini is used as an adjective meaning very small, a sense shared with baby as in a baby car.

clue.text: Governor's outings around British Islands

indicators.note: the governor and outings go around the abbreviation for British

parts.note: a governor is addressed as His Excellency, HE; the 's is a link
rides are trips or outings

explanation.surface: A governor's trips take in Britain's islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container; HE (His Excellency) is crossword shorthand for a governor. The Hebrides are islands off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are an archipelago off Scotland, so they are islands.

clue.text: Be eager to deal with expression of disappointment

parts.note: to long for something is to be eager for it
to face a problem is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Being too keen to tackle things may leave one looking let down.
explanation.definitionFit: A long face is a gloomy expression showing dismay or sadness.

clue.text: Salmon mate

definitions.meaning: a friend or pal, British slang for a close companion

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a Pacific salmon species and an informal term for a friend.

clue.text: Sort of gent to be bred

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A certain kind of gentleman is destined to be well raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges GENT TO BE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Begotten is the past participle of beget, to father offspring, so it means bred.

clue.text: Writer's block is endless

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so this reads 'the writer is'

indicators.note: the word for block loses its last letter

parts.note: a barrier blocks the way

explanation.surface: An author's creative block will never end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final R from BARRIER. J. M. Barrie wrote Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie was a Scottish author, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Sweet little creature captivated son

indicators.note: the creature holds the son captive inside it

parts.note: a mouse is a small animal

explanation.surface: A cute small animal charmed a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivated' puts S inside MOUSE. 'Sweet' looks like an adjective but is a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousse is a light whipped dessert, a sweet course.

clue.text: Everton wingers scoff about a shot taking effort

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so they are the outermost letters of the word
the word for scoff goes around the clue's own a

parts.note: to scoff food is to devour it greedily
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everton's wide players wolf down food after a hard-earned shot on goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is an English football club. 'wingers' gives E and N; 'about' puts A inside DEVOUR to make DEAVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is a strenuous attempt, a try or shot that takes effort.

clue.text: Lizard in attempt to cross floor after head's chopped off

indicators.note: the attempt's word stretches across, enclosing the shortened floor

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt

indicators.note: the word for floor loses its first letter

parts.note: to deck someone is to floor them with a punch

explanation.surface: A lizard tries to scuttle across the floor once its head has been cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after head's chopped off' trims the first letter, and 'to cross' wraps the attempt's word around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A gecko is a small tropical lizard, an example of the creature named.

clue.text: Old note from extremely limited musical performance

indicators.note: the word is limited at its extremes, losing its first and last letters

parts.note: a concert is a musical performance

explanation.surface: An old note from a musical show with a very small audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely limited' trims C and T from CONCERT. A oncer was British slang for a one-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Oncer is old British slang for a one-pound note, which no longer exists.

clue.text: Shrugs off Italian man from start to finish

indicators.note: the first letter is taken from the start and placed at the end

parts.note: signore is the Italian for a gentleman or Mr

explanation.surface: An Italian man brushes things aside all the way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from start to finish' moves the S of SIGNORE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrug something off is to disregard it, which is to pay it no attention.

clue.text: On reflection amusing chap without sex appeal's desperate

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is reversed, so the whole assembly is read backwards
without here means outside, so the chap's word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a card is a joker, an amusing person
it is slang for sex appeal; with the 's it gives its

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a funny man lacking allure is in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' puts the sex-appeal piece inside the chap's word to make CITSARD, and 'On reflection' reverses it. 'Without' reads as lacking but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic and desperate both describe extreme measures taken when things are dire.

clue.text: Expedition leaders ultimately can't stand around

indicators.note: the word for can't stand surrounds the selected letter

parts.note: to be unable to stand something is to hate it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: The heads of a journey can't bear what surrounds them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes S from leaders; 'around' puts HATE around it. 'Expedition' looks like a journey but means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed of action, a less familiar sense meaning hurry.

clue.text: Bound to be seen during festival? One Pearly Queen surely is

indicators.note: the bound's word appears inside the festival's word

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival
a bound is a limit or end

explanation.surface: A Pearly Queen is sure to appear at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be seen during' signals the container. Pearly Kings and Queens are London cockney figures in button-covered clothes; the East End of London is their home area.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearly Queens come from London's working-class east, so one is a person from that district.
